title: TC-01 Early renewal of a single certificate by an authorized operator (AC-1)
precondition:
- A managed certificate on profile Web-Prod whose renewal period has not started (today is before notAfter minus the profile renewal period).
- Renewal is enabled on the profile.
- An RA Operator account holds the early-renewal capability [A: name of the right or permission].
- The certificate has labels, an owner and several SAN entries.
steps:
[1] As the RA Operator, search the certificate in the certificate inventory and open its details

[2] Click Renew [A: label of the early-renewal action]

[3] Confirm the early renewal

[4] If the profile requires approval, approve the request as the approver [A: depends on the enforcement model, see TC-08]

[5] Open the new certificate

[6] Open the previous certificate
expected_results:
[1] The details page shows the certificate as valid, with its expiry date and the profile; the renewal period has not started

[2] A confirmation dialog states that the renewal is outside the renewal period and asks to confirm [A: exact wording]

[3] The request is created without the error WEBRA-RENEW-005 (Certificate not in its renewal period)

[4] The request reaches the completed state

[5] It is issued on profile Web-Prod and the same PKI connector; DN, SAN, extensions, labels, owner and metadata are identical to the previous certificate; only the key may differ

[6] It follows the standard renew handling of the profile (for example revocation or retention as configured)

title: TC-02 Third-party technical metadata is kept on the renewed certificate (AC-1)
precondition:
- A third-party connector is configured and the certificate was deployed through it, with technical data such as an F5 partition Common/prod [A: use a test connector or a stub].
- The certificate is outside its renewal period.
- The operator holds the early-renewal capability.
steps:
[1] Open the certificate details and note the third-party data (connector name, partition or target)

[2] Renew the certificate early

[3] Open the renewed certificate and compare its third-party data

[4] Run the redeployment of the renewed certificate through the connector
expected_results:
[1] The third-party data of the connector is displayed [A: where it appears in the UI and in the API response]

[2] The request succeeds

[3] The connector and the technical data are identical (same partition Common/prod)

[4] It is deployed to the same location as the previous certificate

title: TC-03 Early renewal through the REST API, single and multiple (FR-5, ACT-1)
precondition:
- A Service principal with an API token holding the early-renewal capability.
- Three managed certificates outside their renewal period on the same profile.
steps:
[1] Call the renew endpoint for one certificate without the early-renewal indicator

[2] Call the renew endpoint for the same certificate with the early-renewal indicator [A: name and location of the indicator]

[3] Call the renew endpoint for the two other certificates in one call with the indicator [A: format of the multiple call]

[4] Check the resulting certificates in the inventory
expected_results:
[1] The request is rejected with WEBRA-RENEW-005, as before the change

[2] The request is accepted and a renewal request is created for that certificate

[3] One result per certificate is returned [A: structure of the response]; both renewals are created

[4] Three new certificates exist on the same profile and connector

title: TC-04 Bulk early renewal with a partial failure, from inventory and My Certificates (AC-2)
precondition:
- Ten managed certificates on profile Web-Prod: eight valid outside their renewal period, one revoked, one expired.
- An RA Operator who owns them or can manage them, with the early-renewal capability.
steps:
[1] In the certificate inventory (RA), select the ten certificates with the checkboxes, as for a bulk revocation

[2] Click Renew and confirm the early renewal

[3] Read the outcome of the operation

[4] Check that the eight new certificates still exist after the rejections

[5] Repeat the operation on four other eligible certificates from My Certificates
expected_results:
[1] The selection counter shows 10 and a Renew action is available [A: position of the bulk Renew action]

[2] The confirmation states the renewal is outside the renewal period; processing starts

[3] Eight certificates are renewed; the revoked and the expired certificates are rejected with a per-certificate reason based on status or validity [A: report format and wording]

[4] None of the successful renewals has been rolled back

[5] The same bulk renewal is available and works in My Certificates

title: TC-05 Validity and status checks still apply to early renewal (AC-4)
precondition:
- An authorized operator.
- A revoked certificate, an expired certificate and a certificate on a profile where renewal is not enabled, all outside any renewal period.
steps:
[1] Try an early renewal of the revoked certificate

[2] Try an early renewal of the expired certificate

[3] Try an early renewal of the certificate on the profile without renewal enabled

[4] Check the three certificates
expected_results:
[1] Rejected because of its status; the error is not WEBRA-RENEW-005

[2] Rejected because of its validity; the error is not WEBRA-RENEW-005

[3] Rejected because renewal is not enabled on the profile

[4] None of them was renewed and no new request exists

title: TC-06 Users without the capability cannot renew outside the window (AC-3)
precondition:
- A managed certificate outside its renewal period, owned by an end user.
- The end user can renew in window.
- A privileged user without the early-renewal capability.
steps:
[1] As the end user, open My Certificates and look at the renew action of the certificate

[2] As the end user, call the renew API for this certificate

[3] As the privileged user without the capability, try the early renewal from the UI and the API

[4] Grant the capability to the privileged user and retry
expected_results:
[1] No early-renewal action is offered in self-service [A: Renew hidden, disabled or showing the period error]

[2] Rejected; the certificate is not renewed [A: error code, WEBRA-RENEW-005 or an authorization error]

[3] Rejected; the certificate is not renewed

[4] The early renewal is accepted

title: TC-07 Standard renewals are unchanged (NFR-1, NFR-4, FR-8)
precondition:
- A certificate inside its renewal period owned by an end user.
- A certificate outside its period.
- A certificate linked to an automation policy (metadata AUTOMATION_POLICY).
- Access to the Horizon configuration.
steps:
[1] As the end user, renew the certificate inside its renewal period

[2] Let the automatic renewal run on the certificate outside its period

[3] Renew the automation-policy certificate outside its period with the existing automation bypass

[4] Look for a new global setting in the configuration and in the HOCON files
expected_results:
[1] The renewal succeeds without any early-renewal confirmation

[2] The certificate is not renewed automatically before its period

[3] Behaviour identical to the previous version

[4] No new toggle or HOCON key exists; early renewal is only a per-request action

title: TC-08 Approval workflow for early renewal (ACT-3, FR-8)
precondition:
- [A: the enforcement model is not decided, see Technical Open Question 1] Profile whose renew workflow requires approval.
- An operator who requests early renewals and an RA Operator approver.
- Three certificates outside their renewal period.
steps:
[1] As the operator, request an early renewal of one certificate

[2] As the approver, approve the request

[3] Request another early renewal and deny it as the approver

[4] As the operator, request a bulk early renewal of the three certificates
expected_results:
[1] A request waits for approval and the certificate is not renewed yet [A: depends on the model chosen]

[2] The certificate is renewed

[3] The certificate is not renewed

[4] [A: one request per certificate, or one global request] Each certificate follows the approval workflow independently

title: TC-09 Audit event identifies renewals outside the renewal period (AC-5)
precondition:
- Access to the audit events as a Business administrator.
- One early renewal and one in-window renewal performed.
steps:
[1] Open the audit events and filter on LIFECYCLE-RENEW

[2] Open the event of the early renewal

[3] Open the event of the in-window renewal

[4] Check bulk renewals
expected_results:
[1] Both events are listed

[2] It indicates the renewal occurred outside the renewal period [A: field name or flag] and identifies the operator

[3] It does not carry the out-of-period indication

[4] Each certificate of a bulk early renewal has its own LIFECYCLE-RENEW event with the indication

title: TC-10 Tenant isolation of early renewal (NFR-3)
precondition: - Two tenants A and B, a managed certificate outside its period in tenant B, an operator with the capability in tenant A, and a root tenant administrator.
steps:
[1] As the tenant A operator, try to renew the tenant B certificate through the API with the early-renewal indicator

[2] As the tenant A operator, search the tenant B certificate in the UI

[3] As the root tenant administrator, open the certificate of tenant A
expected_results:
[1] Rejected as not found or forbidden; no request is created

[2] It is not visible

[3] The early-renewal action is visible, as for other lifecycle actions

title: TC-11 Bulk early renewal of several hundred certificates (NFR-2, FR-6)
precondition: - [A: seed of 300 managed certificates outside their period, created by a seed script] An operator with the capability.
steps:
[1] Select the 300 certificates in the inventory and start a bulk early renewal

[2] Follow the progress and wait for the end

[3] Search the new certificates
expected_results:
[1] The screen stays usable; the operation runs asynchronously [A: progress indicator]

[2] All certificates reach a final outcome; the report lists each outcome [A: expected duration threshold, not defined in the spec]

[3] All eligible certificates were renewed, none is duplicated

title: TC-12 Connector migration: repoint the profile then renew early (FR-2, FR-1)
precondition:
- Profile Web-Prod pointing to PKI connector A, with two certificates outside their period.
- A second PKI connector B available.
steps:
[1] Repoint profile Web-Prod to connector B

[2] Renew one certificate early

[3] Look in the renewal UI and API for an option to choose another profile or connector
expected_results:
[1] The profile is saved with connector B

[2] The new certificate is issued by connector B, on profile Web-Prod; the metadata PKI_CONNECTOR shows connector B

[3] None is offered; the renewal always uses the current profile and connector
